text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: oncall_sre_uk paged for P2 - spike in SRV lookup failures and increased application 5xxs from us-west-2b -> possible egress interconnect issue (auto-detected).
oncall_sre_uk: seeing ~25% SRV lookup errors from internal services, correlates with increased connection resets on coredns-egress-usw2b. Investigating.
raj: adding myself. I can tail the coredns logs and check NAT gateway metrics. Which tenants impacted?
lisa: customer telemetry shows service discovery errors for several internal services and a few customer-facing endpoints. CS reported a handful of 502s.
emily: checking infra: network controller shows flaps on the AZ interconnect fabric between us-west-2b and transit-gw, BGP adj change around 2212345600.
jordan: confirmed: BGP flap -> some egress NAT translations stayed sticky and sessions were not rebalanced, causing asymmetric routing and SRV responses timing out.
network-eng: seeing high NAT conn table usage on nat-agg-usw2b-1, many TCP entries in TIME_WAIT, and backend connections from coredns to consul are intermittently failing.
oncall_sre_uk: quick check: `kubectl logs coredns-0 -n kube-system | tail -n 50` shows lots of `read udp` errors and timeouts.
raj: pasting excerpt:
```
[04/Mar/2026:10:34:12 +0000] "[ERROR] read udp 10.0.3.2:53: i/o timeout
[04/Mar/2026:10:34:13 +0000] "[WARN] upstream write failed: connection reset by peer
```

lisa: consul agent on leader node shows increased RPC timeouts, leader election attempts starting at 2212345580. Might be related to SRV lookups failing.
sean: are we seeing cross-AZ routing to standby resolvers? Could explain asymmetric flows.
emily: yes, traffic was flapping between egress in us-west-2b and us-west-2a due to route propagation delay. Some sessions still used stale source IPs (sticky NAT) leading to packet drops.
network-eng: mitigation options: 1) drain and recreate nat-agg-usw2b-1 (disruptive), 2) add route to prefer us-west-2a egress for coredns subnets (fast), 3) force coredns pods to restart to re-establish connections (low blast).
jordan: I'd vote for 2 + 3: prefer quick reroute + restart coredns, monitor if SRV errors drop.
oncall_sre_uk: executing plan: updating route table for cidr 10.0.3.0/24 -> set next-hop to transit-gw-usw2a with higher preference. Applying now. :white_check_mark:
network-eng: route update in progress, propagating via cloud controller.
customer-success-bot: Notifying CS about mitigation and potential impact to customer requests (~5-10min).
raj: restarting coredns daemonset one pod at a time to avoid resolution blips. `kubectl rollout restart -n kube-system daemonset/coredns`
lisa: watch logs and Consul health checks.
emily: route propagated fully at 2212345783 according to controller logs.
sean: coredns restart in progress, first pod back up.
raj: after first pod restart, SRV errors dropped from 26% -> 8% for that node's clients.
oncall_sre_uk: continuing rolling restart, keeping one pod ready.
jordan: also throttling outbound NAT to limit conn table blowups: applied conntrack max per node reduction to 100k.
network-eng: investigating root cause: fabric interconnect had a firmware bug in ARP table aging causing asymmetric forwarding under BGP churn; vendor acknowledged and issued temp config to disable fast-arp on affected spine.
sean: monitoring shows SRV error rate back to baseline ~1.2% after full rollouts and route change. Latency normalized.
lisa: consul leader flaps stopped after coredns restart and egress stabilization; leader has been stable for 15m.
emily: marking mitigation complete in status page. Incident severity reduced to S3.
customer-success-bot: CS updated customers with "Transient service discovery errors in us-west-2b resolved; full mitigation in place. Reach out if you see ongoing issues."
oncall_sre_uk: handoff: I'll be on shift for another 2h, but moving long-tail followups to jordan for postmortem. Assigning postmortem owner: jordan.
jordan: acknowledged. Will gather timeline, config diffs, and vendor comms. Tentative RCA: interconnect ARP/firmware bug + route propagation lag + NAT conn exhaustion -> SRV lookup failures and Consul timeouts.
raj: adding a short-term alert: NAT conn usage > 80% triggers auto-scale or notify. Also adding >=5% SRV error rate to drivebook runbook.
emily: thanks team. Closing incident channel in 30m unless regressions. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident resolution logged. Runbook link: https://playbooks.redwood/az-egress-sticky-nat (auto-generated).
